comments.body:
Root cause established, and it INVERTS the proposed fix. Do not swap the hash.

Measured on this host (macOS 26.6.2, `arm64`), in a worktree venv built by `make venv` +
`make install`:

```
.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc_binary-1.17.dist-info/WHEEL
  Tag: py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64          <- the ARM64 wheel IS the one installed
file .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc/files/pandoc
  Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64          <- but the binary inside it is x86_64
shasum -a 256 <that binary>
  d7b1e75cd20ee6a788a1399492be07d4559949e18e55f34cfc5c91807fdfa90d
```

That hash is EXACTLY the value pinned under `darwin-arm64` in
`scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:60-63`. So the pin is not a copy-paste slip and
it is not internally inconsistent: it faithfully records the binary that
`pypandoc-binary==1.17` actually installs on Apple silicon. The defect is upstream —
the `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel bundles an x86_64 pandoc. The two macOS wheels in `uv.lock`
differ by one byte in size (25553945 vs 25553944), which is consistent with both carrying
the same x86_64 executable.

Consequence: replacing the pin with the genuine arm64 hash
`140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3` would make the
provenance check describe a binary that `uv sync` never installs, so the check would begin
FAILING on arm64 instead of passing. The hash swap alone makes things worse.

The live symptom is not a provenance mismatch but an exec failure, because this host has no
Rosetta:

```
OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable: .../pypandoc/files/pandoc
```

`pypandoc` then falls back, and 17 tests fail in `make verify` on every arm64 Mac:
13 in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py`, 3 in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py`, 1 in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py`.

Verified pre-existing and independent of any source change: a worktree at `origin/main`
(8f7417079ad) carrying only a docs edit fails the same 13 in `test_wiki_render.py`. CI is
unaffected, since the gating cell is `ubuntu-latest` and the linux x86_64 wheel runs
natively — so this never reddens `Verified`, only every local `make verify` on Apple
silicon, which is what makes it expensive.

There is no system pandoc on this host to fall back to (`which pandoc` is empty,
`/opt/homebrew/bin/pandoc` absent).

This now needs a decision rather than a patch, because each option changes the provenance
contract differently. Recorded for the operator; not acting unilaterally.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Plan review BLOCKED — and the measurement says the plan's own fix is backwards

`review_plan` returned **BLOCK** (unsigned, job
`1789911627357418388-b8c9f8b41a3c44a59dbf3eff7eea48bf`). That is correct: the description's
acceptance criteria contradict the root cause recorded in the comment above it. AC1 asks for
the `darwin-arm64` entry to hold a genuine arm64 binary's hash, but the pin already
faithfully records what `uv sync` installs, so swapping it makes the check start FAILING on
arm64 instead of passing.

## New evidence: no version bump can fix this

The prior comment left open whether a different `pypandoc-binary` release ships a real arm64
binary. It does not. Pulled the **latest** release's arm64 wheel straight from PyPI and
inspected the payload:

```
pypandoc_binary-1.17-py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl
  pypandoc/files/pandoc: Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64
  sha256 d7b1e75cd20ee6a788a1399492be07d4559949e18e55f34cfc5c91807fdfa90d
```

That is byte-identical to the value pinned under `darwin-arm64`. And the macOS wheel pair is
the same size in every release back to 1.13, which is what one shared payload looks like:

| version | macosx_10_9_x86_64 | macosx_11_0_arm64 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.13 | 20136798 | 20136798 | 0 |
| 1.14 | 21820896 | 21820899 | 3 |
| 1.15 | 22145734 | 22145735 | 1 |
| 1.16 | 25526415 | 25526415 | 0 |
| 1.16.2 | 25526445 | 25526446 | 1 |
| 1.17 | 25553945 | 25553944 | -1 |

So "bump the dependency" is eliminated by measurement, not by argument. The defect is
upstream in `pypandoc-binary`'s packaging: it publishes an `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel whose
executable is x86_64.

## Why this is a decision and not a patch

Every remaining option changes the provenance contract itself, and they differ in what they
cost and in what guarantee survives:

- Source pandoc differently on darwin-arm64 (a real arm64 binary, e.g. a documented
  system/Homebrew prerequisite) — restores a meaningful byte-safety guarantee, but adds a
  non-Python developer prerequisite and a `uv.lock` change, and the frozen legacy conversion
  outputs for `darwin-arm64` would need regenerating from a pandoc that can actually execute.
- Keep the pin honest and drop the pretence — record that `darwin-arm64` is an x86_64 payload
  and skip the byte-safety claim on that platform, so the check stops asserting something
  untrue.
- Remove the `darwin-arm64` entry entirely and gate the provenance check to platforms where
  it is meaningful (CI's `linux-x86_64`), accepting that Apple silicon has no provenance check.

Each ends with a different answer to the plan's last open question — whether a platform key
may admit more than one acceptable hash — so the description cannot be repaired without the
decision first.

**Not acting unilaterally, and not re-reviewing until the description is rewritten around a
chosen option.** Escalated to the operator. The 17 local `make verify` failures remain
environmental and CI-invisible (the gating cell is `ubuntu-latest`, whose wheel is natively
x86_64), so nothing here is urgent.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`test_the_installed_pandoc_matches_the_legacy_fixture_provenance` fails on every arm64 macOS
host that has a working pandoc configured:

```
ValueError: Pandoc binary SHA-256 mismatch for darwin-arm64:
  expected  d7b1e75cd20ee6a788a1399492be07d4559949e18e55f34cfc5c91807fdfa90d
  installed 140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3
```

- Failing test: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py::test_the_installed_pandoc_matches_the_legacy_fixture_provenance`
- Fails at `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:476`
- Raised from `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:149-152`
- Expectation frozen at `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:60-63`

## Root cause — confirmed by measurement, not inference (re-checked 2026-10-20 on origin/main c0cf1022671)

The `darwin-arm64` entry pins the SHA-256 of an **x86_64** binary.

```
$ file .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc/files/pandoc
Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64
$ shasum -a 256 .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc/files/pandoc
d7b1e75cd20ee6a788a1399492be07d4559949e18e55f34cfc5c91807fdfa90d
```

That is byte-for-byte the value pinned under the `darwin-arm64` key.

The provenance table is:

```python
SUPPORTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256 = {
    "darwin-arm64": "d7b1e75cd20ee6a788a1399492be07d4559949e18e55f34cfc5c91807fdfa90d",
    "linux-x86_64": "decd3dd11a3fe0c16ce56443343ec53adde6fbed6f97d7f56f06b1c424248e7b",
}
```

The platform key is derived from the **host** via `stable_platform_key(system, machine)`, while
the hashed bytes came from the `pypandoc-binary==1.17` wheel payload. That wheel advertises
`macosx_11_0_arm64` but ships an x86_64 executable, so on an arm64 host the key says
`darwin-arm64` and the value is an x86_64 binary's hash.

The introducing commit `11d5994594f` ("deps: bump pypandoc-binary 1.17, ruff 0.16.2") states the
fingerprint was "darwin-arm64 hashed from the installed binary" — which is exactly the mechanism
of the defect. Nothing checked that the installed binary was arm64.

## Why this matters beyond one red test

1. **No genuine arm64 pandoc can ever satisfy the check.** The pinned value is not a real
   arm64 binary's hash, so any correct remedy for `dc28` deterministically fails this test.
2. **The darwin-arm64 byte-safety guarantee is vacuous.** The binary whose hash is pinned
   raises `Bad CPU type in executable` on arm64. Whatever established the frozen conversion
   outputs for that platform key, it was not an executable that runs there.
3. It is a false negative masquerading as provenance: the check passes only while the
   configured pandoc is one that cannot run.

## Decision and evidence (operator, 2026-10-19)

Option (a): accept BOTH fingerprints under `darwin-arm64`. Evidence is in this ticket's comments:
the official jgm/pandoc 3.9 release `pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip` is installed per
`docs/local-dev-env.md:56-64` at `~/.local/pandoc-3.9/pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc` (`file`:
Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64; `--version`: pandoc 3.9; binary sha256
`140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3`). With `PYPANDOC_PANDOC`
pointing at it, all 16 fixture-comparison tests in `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` pass, so the
native binary reproduces `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.json` byte for byte; the only
failure is this provenance check. The Intel value `d7b1e75c…` stays accepted because it is what
the default `pypandoc-binary` wheel installs (it runs under Rosetta).

## Approach

- `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py`: keep `SUPPORTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256` unchanged.
  It is the frozen generating fingerprint map that the committed legacy manifest and the three
  replay fixtures embed and are compared against, so changing its shape would force regenerating
  all four fixture files for no behaviour change. Add `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256`, the set of
  binaries verification accepts per platform: `darwin-arm64` = {Intel `d7b1e75c…`, arm64
  `140353e1…`}, `linux-x86_64` = {`decd3dd1…`}. The installed-binary comparison at `:149-152`
  becomes membership in that set, and its error lists the accepted set sorted. The generating-hash
  check (`:127-132`) uses the same membership, so a future regeneration on a native arm64 host is
  not refused.
- `tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py`: one new test asserting both
  `darwin-arm64` hashes are accepted and a third is rejected with an error naming both accepted
  hashes; the existing validation tests stay unchanged.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md:67-72`: drop the "one test still fails" paragraph (the defect it
  describes is fixed); the install instructions above it stay.
- No fixture file changes (byte identity is proven above).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both fingerprints are accepted under `darwin-arm64`: the new test passes for the Intel and
      the arm64 hash, and rejects a third hash with an error that lists both accepted hashes.
- [ ] Red then green: with `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` set to the native arm64 pandoc,
      `test_the_installed_pandoc_matches_the_legacy_fixture_provenance` fails before the change and
      passes after it (both runs recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] The existing generator validation tests in `tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py`
      pass unchanged, and `git diff` touches no file under `tests/fixtures/`.
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` no longer says a test still fails after the documented setup, and
      `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check` passes.
- [ ] `make verify` with `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` exported finishes with 0 failures.

## Testing

```
export PYPANDOC_PANDOC=$HOME/.local/pandoc-3.9/pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc
.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py -q
make lint && make typecheck && make verify
```
